HG15-p9e2: What is the difference between a human doer and a human being? If you don’t feel good enough as a human being, you will try to become good enough as a human doer by for example being beautiful, doing something well, being smart, having a certain status, being spiritual, etc. I’m not saying those can’t be real gifts, but if failing at one of them feels like losing yourself, then you’re using it to buy belonging.
HG35-forgive-e3: We can not ‘force’ forgiveness on ourselves, it has to come from a place of understanding otherwise it can be bypassing. However, if we remain in the anger forever, we are allowing the injury to dictate how we live our lives in the present. So how do we hold all of this? We just remember that it can all be true at once. They really did hurt us and they still have to answer for it, and our boundary with them still matters, but one day we may find that we have forgiven them.
HG35-quote-e:
A helpful understanding to come to, is that while their actions were harmful, in a sense, they could only make the moves they made, given their accumulated nature at the time (conditioning, history, pain, capacity, etc). This doesn’t negate that harm was caused, holding someone accountable, allowing for consequences, working on making different moves now, etc. It simply helps us come to a place where we aren’t expecting something from someone that they can’t give. It doesn’t make their limitations matter any less.

“You don’t have to forgive before you’re ready. I’m not going to use spirituality to silence your pain, and I also won’t build our whole life around this wound forever.”
HG35-selfforgive-e:
For self-forgiveness, name what you did, but don't take responsibility for what wasn't yours. Let yourself feel the remorse and take in the harm, or how it went against your values, and stop short of making yourself a permanent criminal.

Take responsibility, feel the remorse, then rectify if you can, and then let it go. Be specific about the action you took, and the impact it had, feel the remorse, do what you can to rectify or keep it from happening again, and then stop holding yourself hostage.
